question_text: A hash table stores (key, value) pairs in a fixed-size Python list using open addressing with linear probing. Keys are strings. Do NOT use a Python dict or set. Construct a Python class HashTable with: a constructor __init__(self, capacity) that creates a list called slots of length capacity, with every element None, and a counter count of stored pairs set to 0; a method _hash(self, key) that returns the sum of the Unicode code points (ord) of the characters in key, modulo capacity; a method put(self, key, value) that stores the pair, replacing the value if key is already stored (count must not change in that case); a method get(self, key) that returns the value stored for key, or None if key is not present; and a method load_factor(self) that returns count divided by capacity. You may assume put is never called with a new key when the table is full. Store each pair as a tuple (key, value).
